import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 2

def design(feats):
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    keep = set()
    seen = set()
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if fid1 in seen:
            continue
        keep.add(fid1)
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(feats.ids[i+1:], i+1):
            if fid2 in seen:
                continue
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:,i], feats.x[:,j])[0,1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                seen.add(fid2)
    
    # Calculate effect sizes and select top candidates
    candidates = []
    for fid in keep:
        idx = feats.column(fid)
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, idx]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, idx]
        mean_diff = np.mean(y1) - np.mean(y0)
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)
        candidates.append((fid, abs(mean_diff), abs(t_stat)))
    
    # Sort by effect size
    candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[2], reverse=True)
    
    # Select drivers (top 2)
    drivers = tuple(c[0] for c in candidates[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    
    # Build columns list with all features except near-duplicates
    columns = tuple(c[0] for c in candidates)
    
    # Check for strong correlations to add products
    products = []
    for i, (fid1, _, _) in enumerate(candidates):
        for j, (fid2, _, _) in enumerate(candidates[i+1:], i+1):
            idx1 = feats.column(fid1)
            idx2 = feats.column(fid2)
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:,idx1], feats.x[:,idx2])[0,1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                products.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Create loadings for weighted score (using top feature)
    loadings = {}
    if drivers:
        top_driver = drivers[0]
        idx = feats.column(top_driver)
        # Simple weighting by effect size
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, idx]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, idx]
        mean_diff = np.mean(y1) - np.mean(y0)
        loadings[top_driver] = mean_diff
    
    # Limit total terms to avoid overfitting
    all_terms = len(columns) + len(products) + len(loadings)
    if all_terms > 12:
        # Reduce columns to minimum needed
        columns = columns[:min(6, len(columns))]
        # Keep only products involving features in reduced columns
        products = [(a,b) for a,b in products if a in columns and b in columns]
        # Keep only top loading
        if loadings:
            top_loading = max(loadings.keys(), key=lambda k: abs(loadings[k]))
            loadings = {top_loading: loadings[top_loading]}
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
